chunks: Ali ibn Ahmad ibn Musa (may God be pleased with him) narrated that Ali ibn al-Hasan al-Hassanjani said: Sa'id ibn Kathir ibn Afir narrated to me, from Ibn Lahay'at and Rashdayn ibn Sa'd, from Hurayz ibn Abdullah, from Abu Abd al-Rahman al-Habli, from Abdullah ibn Amr [and] he said: The Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) said during the illness in which he died:

'Call my brother.' So they sent for Ali (peace be upon him). When he entered, the Prophet and Ali turned their faces to the wall and covered themselves with a cloak, and he whispered to him while the people were crowded behind the door. Then Ali (peace be upon him) came out. A man from the people asked him, 'Did the Prophet of God disclose something to you?' He said, 'Yes. He disclosed to me a thousand gates, and in each gate a thousand gates.' The man said, 'Did you memorize them?' He said, 'Yes, and I understood them.' The man said, 'Then what is the blackness in the moon?'

Indeed, God, the Mighty and Exalted, said: 'And We have made the night and the day two signs, so We erased the sign of the night and made the sign of the day visible that you may seek bounty from your Lord and may know the number of years and the account [of time]. And everything We have set in detail.'
The man said to him, 'You truly understood it, O Ali.'

key_terms.آيَتَيْنِ: Two signs (referring to night and day as divine indicators)
key_terms.أَلْفَ بَابٍ: A thousand gates (metaphor for vast knowledge)
key_terms.السَّوَادُ: The blackness (referring to the dark spots on the moon)
key_terms.عَقَلْتُهُ: I understood it (implies deep comprehension beyond mere memorization)

ai.seo_question: What did the Prophet whisper to Ali ibn Abi Talib before his death regarding the signs of the night and day?
ai.summary: In *Al-Khisal*, Shaykh al-Saduq records this narration to illustrate the depth of Ali ibn Abi Talib’s esoteric knowledge (*‘ilm*) received directly from the Prophet during his final illness, a key concept in Shia theology regarding the transmission of divine wisdom. The dialogue highlights Ali’s mastery over both exoteric and esoteric interpretations, as he connects the physical phenomenon of lunar spots to the Quranic verse on the signs of night and day, emphasizing their role in temporal calculation and divine precision. This incident underscores the Shia belief in the Prophet’s private bestowal of comprehensive knowledge upon Ali, distinguishing him as the sole recipient of such profound insights.
